First, we differentiate both sides of the equation with respect to $x,$ assuming that $y=y(x).$

Note that to differentiate the $2xy$ term, we will need to use the product rule.

$$
\begin{aligned}2xy+4{y}^{3} & ={x}^{2}-1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2xy+4{y}^{3}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2xy)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4{y}^{3}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}-1) \\ [2x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y]+12{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+2y+12{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x\end{aligned}
$$

Now we solve the equation for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+12{y}^{2}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =2x-2y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}(2x+12{y}^{2}) & =2x-2y \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2x-2y}{2x+12{y}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x-y}{x+6{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$
